title: MERIDIAN: reference implementation, PayeeBench benchmark, formal models and experiment harness for payee verification in agentic payments
description:
MERIDIAN is a payer-side check that the party about to receive an agent's payment is authorized to receive for the brand the user meant, and that the money went there. This archive contains the reference implementation, the PayeeBench benchmark, Tamarin and ProVerif models, the pre-registrations of hypotheses H1-H5 (and H6 from v2.0.0), and the experiment harness. Running make reproduce regenerates every table and figure from fixed seeds.

Release map: v0.9.0 is a pre-submission snapshot (not peer reviewed; attacks and baselines share one generator; proofs not yet externally reviewed). v1.x accompanies Paper 1, Authority to Receive: Verifiable Payee Chains for Agentic Payments (authority-to-receive verification before authorization). Earlier release notes (v1.0.0, v1.0.1), code comments and results in this archive call the paper by its working title, "Verifiable Discharge"; it is the same paper. v2.x accompanies Paper 2, on post-authorization checks, window-safe scheduling and funded routes. v3.x is reserved for an optional paper on private payee checks. See the paper map in README.md.

The passive web measurement (E10) depends on live DNS, TLS and GLEIF data and gives different numbers on a later run; the archived results record the collection date. Live-backend results were obtained on Stripe test mode and a public testnet only. The Groth16 setup uses fixed test entropy and must not protect real payments.
